```
ccRRcc
cRRRcX
cRRRcX
ccRRcc
```
So the arrow is a 2×2 block (columns 14-15... wait: rows 25-28, columns 14-15 = 2×2, plus a protrusion at rows 26-27, column 13). So the tip is on the left side (column 13). The red arrow on the left points left. The green arrow on the right: columns 47-48 are 2×2, protrusion at rows 26-27, column 46? Let me check: "gcNNNc" — columns 45-50: g c N N N c. So N is at 47, 48, 49? Hmm wait: crop(24,29,45,51): row 26 = "gcNNNc" → column 45=g, 46=c, 47=N, 48=N, 49=N, 50=c. Row 25 = "ccNNcc" → column 47=N, 48=N. So the green arrow: 2×2 at rows 25-26, columns 47-48, plus N at rows 26-27, column 49. The tip is on the right side (column 49). So the green arrow points right.
Top arrows: red (16,20): 2×2 at rows 16-17, columns 20-21, plus R at rows 17-18, column 19 → tip is on the left side (column 19). Points left. Green (16,38): 2×2 at rows 16-17, columns 38-39, plus N at rows 17-18, column 40 → tip is on the right. Points right.
So all red arrows point left, all green arrows point right. Consistent with level 1: red = one direction, green = the opposite direction.
Now, which line does each arrow control? The top arrows are above columns 23/35, but they point left/right (horizontal). Hmm, if the red arrow above column 23 points left... it's positioned above the top end of column 23. If it shifts column 23, the direction should be vertical (up/down). Pointing left suggests it rotates something in the horizontal direction.
New hypothesis: the arrows rotate a ring, and the ring here is the outer 24-tile loop. Red arrow = CCW, green = CW, same as level 1, and all six arrows do the same thing (rotate the whole outer ring)? But then why six?
Or: the arrows control the two horizontal strips (rows 26 and 35) as "rows" that shift left/right with wraparound, and the top arrows control the two vertical columns (23, 35) that shift up/down... but the top arrows point horizontally.
Hmm, wait. Maybe the top arrows also control rows: red (16,20) is above the top-left region... row 17! The top row (row 17) has tiles at columns 23-35. The red arrow at (16,20) is above the left end of row 17, pointing left → shifts row 17 left. The green arrow at (16,38) is above the right end of row 17, pointing right → shifts row 17 right. That makes sense!
Similarly, the bottom row (row 44) has no arrows. And rows 26/35 have left/right arrows. So the arrows control rows: row 17 (red on left, green on right), row 26 (red on left, green on right), row 35 (red on left, green on right). But what about row 44 and the columns? The Y tiles are at (17,32) [row 17] and (38,23) [column 23]. The marker boxes are at (26,35) and (35,35) [column 35].
If only rows can shift, then the Y at (38,23) can never reach column 35. Unless the columns also shift. Hmm.
Maybe the arrows rotate the entire outer ring (24 tiles), and the row arrows shift the inner strips? Let me probe: click the red arrow at (25,14) and take a diff. That's the decisive test. If the whole outer ring rotates CCW, the top row moves left, the left column moves down, etc. If only row 26 shifts left, then only the tiles in row 26 move.
Let's probe.
